title: A number that exactly matches one Part Library entry links to it
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin who can switch between two locations, the test location and location B, so a part can be stocked at location B only.
  • Create a part for this test at location B only, part A, with a description, description 1, so its Part Library entry exists and part A is not stocked at the test location.
  • Use a description, description 2, that differs from description 1 by more than upper and lower case.
  • Start on the Inventory page (Parts in the top bar, then Inventory in the left menu), on the Active tab.
custom_steps:
1. Click New Inventory Part.
  2. Type description 2 in the Description field.
  3. Type part A's part number in the Part Number field, with the same upper and lower case.
  4. Pick any category in the Category field.
  5. Type 10.00 in the Cost field.
  6. Click Save.
  7. Type part A's part number in the Search box.
  8. Click Part Library in the left menu.
  9. Type part A's part number in the Search box.
  10. Click the part A row.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • The New Inventory Part window opens.

Step 2:

  • Description reads description 2.

Step 3:

  • Part Number reads part A's part number.

Step 4:

  • The category shows in the Category field.

Step 5:

  • Cost reads $10.00.

Step 6:

  • The window closes.
  • A green message reads: Part created. Linked to (part A's part number) in the Part Library. Its description "(description 1)" was kept.
  • The message goes away on its own.

Step 7:

  • One row is listed for part A, with description 1 (the Part Library entry's description), not description 2.

Step 8:

  • The Part Library page opens.

Step 9:

  • Exactly one entry is listed for part A's number, still with description 1: no second entry was made.

Step 10:

  • The entry's detail page lists part A at both the test location and location B.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Parts Lifecycle Update", Confluence 829227015, version 33 (23 Oct 2026, owner Chris Ward), read 27 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-10647, story SV-10820 (Story 7, Create a Part by Typing Its Number and Description)

  • S7-R4: “On save, the system looks for a Part Library entry whose number is exactly the number typed, including upper and lower case.”
  • S7-R5: “If exactly one entry matches, the new part is linked to that entry.”
  • S7-R6: “A linked entry keeps its own description. The description typed in the dialog does not change it.”
  • S7-R9: “When the part was linked to an existing entry whose description differs from the one typed, ignoring upper and lower case and spaces before and after, the system shows "Part created. Linked to {part number} in the Part Library. Its description "{library description}" was kept." For example: "Part created. Linked to N68SL-356 in the Part Library. Its description "BRAKE PAD" was kept."”
  • User Feedback Summary: “New part linked to an entry whose description differs | "Part created. Linked to {part number} in the Part Library. Its description "{library description}" was kept." | Success toast, fades on its own”
  • Key Decisions: “In the New Inventory Part dialog, a new part links to an existing Part Library entry only on an exact match. Exact means the same characters, including upper and lower case. Any other number gets an entry of its own. A near match is never linked, because two different products can share a number that differs only in punctuation, and linking them would merge them.”

The build is not yet available to check this case against.
